artists.name: Maya Chen
artists.tagline: Colour fields for rooms people actually live in.
artists.bio: Maya paints large, quiet abstractions built from thin acrylic washes — twenty or thirty layers, each one almost transparent. She started making them after five years designing hospital interiors, where she learned that a wall can either raise your heart rate or lower it. Her work is an argument for the second option.

artists.name: Jordan Williams
artists.tagline: The city after everyone has gone home.
artists.bio: Jordan shoots long exposures on the South Side between two and five in the morning, when the streetlights are the only thing moving. He works with a tripod, a stopwatch and no digital correction — what the sensor collects in ninety seconds is what you get. He also keeps a stencil practice, which he insists is the same project by other means.

artists.name: Sofia Martinez
artists.tagline: High desert light, one broken stroke at a time.
artists.bio: Sofia paints the ninety minutes before sundown outside Santa Fe, and only that. She builds each canvas from thousands of short unblended strokes, so the colour mixes in your eye rather than on the palette. She has painted the same three mesas for eleven years and says she is not finished with them.

artists.name: Ethan Brooks
artists.tagline: Removing things until only the decision is left.
artists.bio: Ethan makes work with one or two marks on it, which takes him considerably longer than that sounds. He trained as a bookbinder, and the discipline shows: hand-torn cotton rag, visible deckle, nothing centred. He describes his practice as editing rather than drawing.

artists.name: Ava Patel
artists.tagline: Portraits of people who are not quite there.
artists.bio: Ava builds faces out of overlapping flat planes, then removes enough of them that the sitter stays anonymous. The people are real — friends, neighbours, her grandmother — but she paints only what she can remember of them a week later. Recently the rooms behind them have started behaving strangely.

artists.name: Noah Kim
artists.bio: Noah composes on graph paper before he touches paint, and never deviates from the plan. Circles, quarter-arcs, a single rule dividing the field — the vocabulary has not changed since 2019 and he considers that the point. He masks every edge by hand because tape leaves a better line than a steady wrist.

artists.name: Layla Thompson
artists.tagline: Fog, ridgelines, and the twenty minutes they overlap.
artists.bio: Layla walks the Blue Ridge before dawn with a medium-format camera and comes back with maybe one usable frame. She prints on matte cotton so the blacks stay soft, because the mountains are never as contrasty as a screen makes them look. She has never photographed a person on purpose.

artists.name: Daniel Rivera
artists.bio: Daniel screenprints in four flat colours and no gradients, using a halftone screen he cut himself in 2016 and refuses to replace. He came out of skate-shop graphics and gig posters, and it shows in the register — everything is meant to be legible from across a room. He thinks most contemporary art is too quiet to be honest.

artists.name: Amara Johnson
artists.tagline: Paper with a history, cut up and put back.
artists.bio: Amara works with ledger paper, dress patterns and letters bought by the pound at estate sales in south Atlanta. She tears rather than cuts, layers with wheat paste, then draws over the whole surface in walnut ink. Her grandmother taught her the quilting logic underneath it, which she says is the only formal training that mattered.

artists.name: Leo Zhang
artists.tagline: One gesture, loaded brush, no second attempt.
artists.bio: Leo grinds his own ink and works standing, finishing each piece in a single pass — if the stroke is wrong, the sheet goes in the bin. He trained in calligraphy in Hangzhou and spent a decade unlearning the characters until only the movement was left. He makes roughly forty pieces a year and keeps four.

artworks.title: Blue Horizon
artworks.description: A single band of deep blue settles across the lower third, carried on thirty-one washes of thinned acrylic. Up close the surface is almost entirely edge; from across a room it reads as one uninterrupted breath of colour.
artworks.artist_note: I painted this the week my father came out of hospital. I wanted something that lowered the room instead of asking anything of it.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (colorField, seed “blue-horizon”).
artworks.alt_text: Blue Horizon by Maya Chen — Acrylic on canvas, abstract and contemporary

artworks.title: Tidal Register
artworks.description: Blue-green washes stack in uneven horizontal registers, each one recording where the previous layer had already dried. Marble dust gives the upper field a chalky tooth that catches side light.
artworks.artist_note: The bands are not planned. They are the tide line of whatever I did the day before.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (colorField, seed “tidal-register”).
artworks.alt_text: Tidal Register by Maya Chen — Acrylic on canvas, abstract

artworks.title: Slow Water
artworks.description: A square of pale blue that darkens almost imperceptibly toward one corner. The only incident is a soft-edged form near the centre, more suggestion than shape.
artworks.artist_note: Made to be looked at for a long time, or not at all. Both are fine.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (colorField, seed “slow-water”).
artworks.alt_text: Slow Water by Maya Chen — Acrylic on panel, abstract and contemporary

artworks.title: Ninety Layers
artworks.description: Ochre and raw umber built up over four months until the surface stopped being paint and started being ground. A single dark gesture crosses the field just below centre.
artworks.artist_note: I counted for a while and then stopped. Ninety is a guess.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (colorField, seed “ninety-layers”).
artworks.alt_text: Ninety Layers by Maya Chen — Acrylic on canvas, abstract

artworks.title: Field Notes, Morning
artworks.description: A small study in warm grey and pale sage, made in a single sitting before the light changed. The paper edge is left visible.
artworks.artist_note: One of about forty of these. They are how I decide what the big ones are going to be.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (colorField, seed “field-notes-morning”).
artworks.alt_text: Field Notes, Morning by Maya Chen — Acrylic on paper, abstract

artworks.title: Terracotta Interval
artworks.description: Burnt orange and clay, held apart by a band of near-white that does not quite reach either edge. Cold wax gives the whole surface a matte, plastered quality.
artworks.artist_note: The gap in the middle is the piece. Everything else is there to make the gap possible.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (colorField, seed “terracotta-interval”).
artworks.alt_text: Terracotta Interval by Maya Chen — Oil on canvas, abstract and contemporary

artworks.title: The Long Wash
artworks.description: Six feet of graduated blue, poured in one continuous pass on a levelled floor and left to find its own edges over nine days. The largest single-pour work she has completed.
artworks.artist_note: You get one attempt. I ruined four canvases before this one behaved.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (colorField, seed “the-long-wash”).
artworks.alt_text: The Long Wash by Maya Chen — Acrylic on canvas, abstract

artworks.title: Verdigris
artworks.description: Oxidised greens over a warm grey ground, with copper pigment worked into the upper edge so the colour shifts as you walk past it.
artworks.artist_note: Named for the roof of the building where I had my first studio.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (colorField, seed “verdigris”).
artworks.alt_text: Verdigris by Maya Chen — Acrylic on panel, abstract and contemporary

artworks.title: 3:14 AM, Wabash
artworks.description: Ninety seconds under the elevated tracks. Sodium light drags into long amber ribbons across an otherwise black frame; the girders stay perfectly still.
artworks.artist_note: No correction, no stacking. What the sensor collected in ninety seconds is what you are looking at.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (lightStudy, seed “3-14-am-wabash”).
artworks.alt_text: 3:14 AM, Wabash by Jordan Williams — Archival pigment print, photography

artworks.title: Nightwork
artworks.description: A cold blue cast over near-total darkness, broken by three vertical filaments of light where a service crew worked through the night.
artworks.artist_note: They let me stand there for two hours. Nobody asked what I was doing.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (lightStudy, seed “nightwork”).
artworks.alt_text: Nightwork by Jordan Williams — Archival pigment print, photography

artworks.title: Ninety Seconds
artworks.description: The exposure that gave the series its name. Headlights on a wet road resolve into a single sweeping arc, bright enough to read as a physical object.
artworks.artist_note: I timed it on a kitchen stopwatch. Still do.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (lightStudy, seed “ninety-seconds”).
artworks.alt_text: Ninety Seconds by Jordan Williams — Archival pigment print, photography

artworks.title: Cut Piece No. 4
artworks.description: A hand-cut radial stencil laid over two passes of red, with the overspray left in. The plywood grain shows through where the paint went thin.
artworks.artist_note: Cut the stencil with a scalpel over three evenings. Used it once, then it fell apart.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (stencil, seed “cut-piece-no-4”).
artworks.alt_text: Cut Piece No. 4 by Jordan Williams — Spray paint and stencil on panel, street art and contemporary
artworks.medium: Spray paint and stencil on panel

artworks.title: Overspray
artworks.description: Four stencil layers in fluorescent red and orange, deliberately misregistered. Drips are left where they fell.
artworks.artist_note: The misregistration is the whole point. A clean print of this would be worthless.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (stencil, seed “overspray”).
artworks.alt_text: Overspray by Jordan Williams — Aerosol on canvas, street art

artworks.title: Stencil Study (Red)
artworks.description: A small, fast study — one stencil, one colour, three minutes. The speckle at the edges is where the can was held too close.
artworks.artist_note: These are warm-ups. I have hundreds. This one I liked.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (stencil, seed “stencil-study-red”).
artworks.alt_text: Stencil Study (Red) by Jordan Williams — Aerosol on paper, street art

artworks.title: Lake Shore, Long
artworks.description: A four-minute exposure of Lake Michigan in February. The water has gone completely smooth; only the horizon and a single distant light survive the length of the frame.
artworks.artist_note: It was eleven degrees. The battery died right after this one.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (lightStudy, seed “lake-shore-long”).
artworks.alt_text: Lake Shore, Long by Jordan Williams — Archival pigment print, photography

artworks.title: Mesa, Six O’Clock
artworks.description: The west mesa at the exact moment the rock turns from orange to violet, built from several thousand short unblended strokes. The colour mixes in your eye, not on the palette.
artworks.artist_note: Ninety minutes a day, eleven days. On the twelfth it rained and I stopped.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (pointillist, seed “mesa-six-oclock”).
artworks.alt_text: Mesa, Six O’Clock by Sofia Martinez — Oil on linen, impressionist and landscape

artworks.title: Chamisa in Flower
artworks.description: A field of yellow chamisa in late September, painted so densely that the ground barely shows. Small strokes of sage and dusty green hold the yellow from going flat.
artworks.artist_note: It smells appalling in bloom. The colour makes up for it.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (pointillist, seed “chamisa-in-flower”).
artworks.alt_text: Chamisa in Flower by Sofia Martinez — Oil on panel, impressionist

artworks.title: Arroyo, After Rain
artworks.description: The dry wash behind her studio, briefly running. Wet sand takes on a green cast that lasts about two hours a year.
artworks.artist_note: I have waited for this four times and got it twice.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (pointillist, seed “arroyo-after-rain”).
artworks.alt_text: Arroyo, After Rain by Sofia Martinez — Oil on linen, impressionist and landscape

artworks.title: The Same Three Mesas
artworks.description: Six feet of high desert at the end of the day, the culmination of eleven years spent on one view. Three ridgelines recede into violet; the foreground stays hot.
artworks.artist_note: People ask when I will paint something else. I do not have an answer they like.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (strata, seed “the-same-three-mesas”).
artworks.alt_text: The Same Three Mesas by Sofia Martinez — Oil on linen, landscape and impressionist

artworks.title: Piñon Shadow
artworks.description: A quiet study of shadow under a piñon at midday, where the ground goes blue-green in the shade and bone-pale two inches away.
artworks.artist_note: Painted sitting on a rock. There is a bit of the rock in the paint.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (pointillist, seed “pi-on-shadow”).
artworks.alt_text: Piñon Shadow by Sofia Martinez — Gouache on paper, impressionist

artworks.title: Last Light, Tesuque
artworks.description: The hottest painting in the series — cadmium orange and lemon laid side by side with almost no mixing, so the whole canvas vibrates at the edges.
artworks.artist_note: The last four minutes before the sun goes behind the ridge. You do not get to plan.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (strata, seed “last-light-tesuque”).
artworks.alt_text: Last Light, Tesuque by Sofia Martinez — Oil on linen, landscape and impressionist

artworks.title: Snow on Sangre de Cristo
artworks.description: First snow on the range, painted from a parking lot. Warm greys in the foreground give way to a cold violet at the peaks.
artworks.artist_note: Small, because it was too cold to stand there for long.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (strata, seed “snow-on-sangre-de-cristo”).
artworks.alt_text: Snow on Sangre de Cristo by Sofia Martinez — Oil on panel, landscape

artworks.title: Rule, Interrupted
artworks.description: One horizontal rule, drawn in a single pass, stopping four inches short of the right edge. Nothing else is on the sheet.
artworks.artist_note: The version where the line reaches the edge took two seconds longer and was much worse.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (minimal, seed “rule-interrupted”).
artworks.alt_text: Rule, Interrupted by Ethan Brooks — Ink on cotton rag, minimalist
artworks.materials: Sumi ink on hand-torn cotton rag

artworks.title: Two Decisions
artworks.description: A short rule and a single dot, placed off-centre in both directions. The deckle edge is left raw on all four sides.
artworks.artist_note: Two marks. It took most of a week to decide where the second one went.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (minimal, seed “two-decisions”).
artworks.alt_text: Two Decisions by Ethan Brooks — Ink on cotton rag, minimalist
artworks.materials: Sumi ink, cotton rag, deckle edge

artworks.title: Deckle No. 9
artworks.description: Three torn rectangles of undyed rag, overlapped and pasted, with a faint graphite line running underneath all three.
artworks.artist_note: The tear is the drawing. I stopped pretending otherwise around 2022.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (collage, seed “deckle-no-9”).
artworks.alt_text: Deckle No. 9 by Ethan Brooks — Collage on rag, mixed media and minimalist

artworks.title: Everything Removed
artworks.description: A four-foot field of warm off-white with a single hairline division low on the left. The quietest work in his practice, and the largest.
artworks.artist_note: There were nine other elements. I took them all out over about five months.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (minimal, seed “everything-removed”).
artworks.alt_text: Everything Removed by Ethan Brooks — Acrylic on canvas, minimalist

artworks.title: Fold, Twice
artworks.description: The sheet was folded twice before it was drawn on, and the ink stopped where the creases were. The folds are the composition.
artworks.artist_note: Bookbinding does this to you. You start seeing the paper as the work.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (minimal, seed “fold-twice”).
artworks.alt_text: Fold, Twice by Ethan Brooks — Ink on paper, minimalist and mixed media

artworks.title: Margin
artworks.description: A pale field with a narrow band of cold blue holding the left quarter. Nothing is centred, and nothing is quite where you expect it.
artworks.artist_note: Named after the part of a page nobody looks at, which is where I put everything.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (minimal, seed “margin”).
artworks.alt_text: Margin by Ethan Brooks — Acrylic on panel, minimalist

artworks.title: Neighbour, Remembered
artworks.description: A head built from six overlapping flat planes in oxide red and umber. The features never resolve, but the posture is unmistakable.
artworks.artist_note: He lived across the hall for four years. I painted him from memory a week after he moved out.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (figure, seed “neighbour-remembered”).
artworks.alt_text: Neighbour, Remembered by Ava Patel — Acrylic on panel, portrait and contemporary
artworks.materials: Acrylic and oil stick on birch

artworks.title: My Grandmother, Twice
artworks.description: Two overlapping profiles of the same woman, painted a year apart and eventually resolved onto one panel. The violet ground belonged to the second sitting.
artworks.artist_note: The second one is more accurate. The first one is more her.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (figure, seed “my-grandmother-twice”).
artworks.alt_text: My Grandmother, Twice by Ava Patel — Oil on panel, portrait
artworks.materials: Oil and oil stick on panel

artworks.title: Sitter with No Room
artworks.description: A figure seated in a space that does not close — the horizon runs behind her at two different heights, and her shadow falls toward the light.
artworks.artist_note: The backgrounds started misbehaving about a year ago. I decided to let them.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (dreamscape, seed “sitter-with-no-room”).
artworks.alt_text: Sitter with No Room by Ava Patel — Acrylic on canvas, surrealist and portrait

artworks.title: Plane, Face, Plane
artworks.description: A small study: three planes, one of which happens to be a face. Removing the fourth is what made it work.
artworks.artist_note: These studies are how I find out whether a person is going to hold up at size.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (figure, seed “plane-face-plane”).
artworks.alt_text: Plane, Face, Plane by Ava Patel — Acrylic on panel, portrait and contemporary

artworks.title: The Room Behaves
artworks.description: A domestic interior in violet and burnt orange where a doorway stands unattached in open floor, casting a shadow four times its own length.
artworks.artist_note: Titled optimistically. It does not.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (dreamscape, seed “the-room-behaves”).
artworks.alt_text: The Room Behaves by Ava Patel — Acrylic on canvas, surrealist
artworks.materials: Acrylic and oil stick on canvas

artworks.title: Anonymous (Blue)
artworks.description: The quietest portrait in the series. Cool blue planes over a grey ground; the sitter is turned almost entirely away.
artworks.artist_note: She asked not to be recognisable. That turned out to improve it.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (figure, seed “anonymous-blue”).
artworks.alt_text: Anonymous (Blue) by Ava Patel — Acrylic on panel, portrait and contemporary

artworks.title: Six Faces, One Week
artworks.description: Her largest work: six sitters from a single week, painted from memory the following Sunday, overlapping across five and a half feet of canvas.
artworks.artist_note: By the end of the week I could not tell you which features belonged to whom. That is in the painting.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (figure, seed “six-faces-one-week”).
artworks.alt_text: Six Faces, One Week by Ava Patel — Acrylic on canvas, portrait and contemporary
artworks.materials: Acrylic and oil stick on canvas

artworks.title: Quarter Arc, Cadmium
artworks.description: A cadmium quarter-arc springing from the lower-left corner into a lemon field, with one thin rule dividing the upper third.
artworks.artist_note: Graph paper first, always. If the drawing is wrong the painting cannot save it.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (hardEdge, seed “quarter-arc-cadmium”).
artworks.alt_text: Quarter Arc, Cadmium by Noah Kim — Acrylic on birch panel, contemporary

artworks.title: Graph Paper No. 22
artworks.description: Four rectangles and one circle on a five-by-five grid, in slate blue and near-black. The grid is never drawn, only obeyed.
artworks.artist_note: Number 22 of an ongoing set. Most of them do not get painted.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (hardEdge, seed “graph-paper-no-22”).
artworks.alt_text: Graph Paper No. 22 by Noah Kim — Acrylic on birch panel, contemporary and abstract

artworks.title: Two Circles, One Rule
artworks.description: Two discs of unequal size, one cropped by the frame, separated by a single vertical rule that is not quite at the golden section.
artworks.artist_note: It is off by about an inch on purpose. On the section it looked smug.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (hardEdge, seed “two-circles-one-rule”).
artworks.alt_text: Two Circles, One Rule by Noah Kim — Acrylic on birch panel, contemporary

artworks.title: Masked by Hand
artworks.description: A small yellow field cut by three black bars at unequal spacing. Every edge is masked by hand, and the slight thickness variation is visible up close.
artworks.artist_note: Tape leaves a better line than a steady wrist. I have tested this extensively.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (hardEdge, seed “masked-by-hand”).
artworks.alt_text: Masked by Hand by Noah Kim — Acrylic on panel, contemporary and abstract

artworks.title: Division
artworks.description: Five feet of black and off-white split by one hard vertical, with a single cadmium arc breaking the seam near the base. His largest and most severe work.
artworks.artist_note: The arc is the only thing I changed after the drawing. It needed one mistake.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (hardEdge, seed “division”).
artworks.alt_text: Division by Noah Kim — Acrylic on canvas, contemporary

artworks.title: Blue Field, Two Arcs
artworks.description: A soft slate-blue ground with two pale quarter-arcs at opposite corners. The gentlest painting he has made, and the only one without a rule.
artworks.artist_note: Someone asked for a quiet one. This is what that looks like from me.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (hardEdge, seed “blue-field-two-arcs”).
artworks.alt_text: Blue Field, Two Arcs by Noah Kim — Acrylic on birch panel, contemporary and abstract

artworks.title: Ferry Light
artworks.description: A single navigation light on flat water at first light, printed on matte cotton so the blacks stay open and soft.
artworks.artist_note: Taken from a dock at 5:20. The light went out about a minute later.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (lightStudy, seed “ferry-light”).
artworks.alt_text: Ferry Light by Layla Thompson — Archival pigment print, photography and landscape

artworks.title: Ridge, 5:40
artworks.description: Four ridgelines fading into morning fog, each one a shade paler than the last. There is no black anywhere in the frame.
artworks.artist_note: The mountains are never as contrasty as a screen makes them look. I print for the mountains.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (lightStudy, seed “ridge-5-40”).
artworks.alt_text: Ridge, 5:40 by Layla Thompson — Archival pigment print, photography and landscape

artworks.title: Fog Bank
artworks.description: Almost nothing: a horizontal band of grey where a valley should be, and one darker mark near the lower edge that turns out to be a tree.
artworks.artist_note: I stood there for forty minutes waiting for it to clear. It did not, which was better.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (lightStudy, seed “fog-bank”).
artworks.alt_text: Fog Bank by Layla Thompson — Archival pigment print, photography

artworks.title: Twenty Minutes
artworks.description: The twenty minutes when fog and ridgeline overlap and neither one wins. Printed large enough that the grain in the fog becomes part of the surface.
artworks.artist_note: The whole series is about this window. It happens maybe nine mornings a year.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (strata, seed “twenty-minutes”).
artworks.alt_text: Twenty Minutes by Layla Thompson — Archival pigment print, landscape and photography

artworks.title: Cove, No Wind
artworks.description: Still water in a small cove, with the far bank reflected so exactly that the horizon has to be inferred.
artworks.artist_note: Small on purpose. It does not need to be big to do what it does.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (lightStudy, seed “cove-no-wind”).
artworks.alt_text: Cove, No Wind by Layla Thompson — Archival pigment print, photography and landscape

artworks.title: Blue Ridge, Matte
artworks.description: Six feet of the Blue Ridge at the moment the blue is literal. Seven receding ranges, printed at a size where each one holds its own detail.
artworks.artist_note: Eleven trips before I got a morning clear enough to justify printing it this large.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (strata, seed “blue-ridge-matte”).
artworks.alt_text: Blue Ridge, Matte by Layla Thompson — Archival pigment print, landscape and photography
artworks.materials: Archival pigment on matte cotton rag

artworks.title: Loud On Purpose
artworks.description: Four flat colours, no gradients, one hand-cut halftone screen. A red disc sits dead centre and refuses to apologise for it.
artworks.artist_note: I cut that halftone screen in 2016 and I will not be replacing it.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (halftone, seed “loud-on-purpose”).
artworks.alt_text: Loud On Purpose by Daniel Rivera — Four-colour screenprint, pop art

artworks.title: Four Flats
artworks.description: Lemon and cobalt in four flat bands under a rotated dot screen. Legible from thirty feet, which is the entire specification.
artworks.artist_note: If you have to walk up to it, I did it wrong.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (halftone, seed “four-flats”).
artworks.alt_text: Four Flats by Daniel Rivera — Four-colour screenprint, pop art and contemporary

artworks.title: Halftone Sun
artworks.description: Concentric orange rings under a coarse dot screen, printed slightly out of register so the edges buzz.
artworks.artist_note: The buzz is the register error. I print them one at a time and do not correct it.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (halftone, seed “halftone-sun”).
artworks.alt_text: Halftone Sun by Daniel Rivera — Three-colour screenprint, pop art

artworks.title: Gig Poster (Never Printed)
artworks.description: A poster design for a show that was cancelled, enlarged onto panel and finished by hand in fluorescent violet and orange.
artworks.artist_note: The band broke up two days before the run. The artwork was the only thing that survived.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (halftone, seed “gig-poster-never-printed”).
artworks.alt_text: Gig Poster (Never Printed) by Daniel Rivera — Acrylic and screenprint on panel, pop art and street art

artworks.title: The Door Was Not There

artworks.artist_note: Somebody told me pop art cannot be strange. This is my response.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (dreamscape, seed “the-door-was-not-there”).
artworks.alt_text: The Door Was Not There by Daniel Rivera — Acrylic on canvas, surrealist and pop art

artworks.title: Register

artworks.title: Dress Pattern (Sunday)
artworks.description: Tissue dress-pattern pieces laid over oxide red, with the cutting lines and notches left legible under the ink.
artworks.artist_note: My grandmother made a version of this dress. I found the pattern in an estate sale two miles from her house.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (collage, seed “dress-pattern-sunday”).
artworks.alt_text: Dress Pattern (Sunday) by Amara Johnson — Collage on panel, mixed media and traditional
artworks.materials: Found tissue pattern, wheat paste, ink, panel

artworks.title: Walnut Ink Study
artworks.description: A branch study in home-made walnut ink, which starts warm brown and goes almost black where it pools.
artworks.artist_note: I make the ink from the tree in my mother’s yard. It gets darker every year.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (ink, seed “walnut-ink-study”).
artworks.alt_text: Walnut Ink Study by Amara Johnson — Walnut ink on paper, traditional

artworks.title: Quilt Logic
artworks.description: A nine-block structure borrowed from quilting, built entirely from torn paper in oxide red and dusty green and drawn back into with ink.
artworks.artist_note: The only formal training that mattered. She never called it composition.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (collage, seed “quilt-logic”).
artworks.alt_text: Quilt Logic by Amara Johnson — Collage and ink on canvas, mixed media and traditional
artworks.materials: Found paper, wheat paste, walnut ink, canvas

artworks.title: Letters, Bought by the Pound
artworks.description: Five feet of layered correspondence — none of it legible, all of it real — pasted, sanded back, and unified under a wash of walnut ink.
artworks.artist_note: I read every letter before I tore it. That felt like the minimum.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (collage, seed “letters-bought-by-the-pound”).
artworks.alt_text: Letters, Bought by the Pound by Amara Johnson — Collage and ink on canvas, mixed media

artworks.title: Branch, Walnut
artworks.description: A single branch with seven leaves, drawn wet-into-wet so the ink pools at each junction. A green wash sits underneath.
artworks.artist_note: Seven leaves because the eighth one made it a decoration.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (ink, seed “branch-walnut”).
artworks.alt_text: Branch, Walnut by Amara Johnson — Walnut ink on paper, traditional

artworks.title: One Pass
artworks.description: One vertical stroke, four feet long, made standing, in a single unbroken movement. Where the brush ran dry, it was allowed to run dry.
artworks.artist_note: If the stroke is wrong the sheet goes in the bin. This is the fourth sheet.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (minimal, seed “one-pass”).
artworks.alt_text: One Pass by Leo Zhang — Sumi ink on Xuan paper, minimalist and abstract
artworks.materials: Hand-ground sumi ink on Xuan paper

artworks.title: Kept (No. 3 of 40)
artworks.description: Two short strokes crossing near the lower third, with a dry-brush tail on the second. Ink density shifts across the sheet where the paper drank unevenly.
artworks.artist_note: I make about forty pieces a year and keep four. This was the third one I kept.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (minimal, seed “kept-no-3-of-40”).
artworks.alt_text: Kept (No. 3 of 40) by Leo Zhang — Sumi ink on Xuan paper, minimalist
artworks.materials: Hand-ground sumi ink on Xuan paper

artworks.title: Unlearning
artworks.description: A mark that was a character ten years ago and is now only a movement. Small, and deliberately unresolved.
artworks.artist_note: A decade removing the meaning until the gesture was the only thing left.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (minimal, seed “unlearning”).
artworks.alt_text: Unlearning by Leo Zhang — Sumi ink on Xuan paper, minimalist and abstract

artworks.title: Loaded Brush
artworks.description: A fully loaded brush dragged once across four feet of canvas over a cold blue ground, spending its entire charge of ink in the first eighteen inches.
artworks.artist_note: On canvas the ink behaves completely differently. It took two years to stop fighting that.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (minimal, seed “loaded-brush”).
artworks.alt_text: Loaded Brush by Leo Zhang — Sumi ink and acrylic on canvas, minimalist and abstract
artworks.medium: Sumi ink and acrylic on canvas

artworks.title: Standing Work
artworks.description: Nearly six feet of paper with three marks on it, made in one pass over about eleven seconds. The largest sheet he can reach across without stepping.
artworks.artist_note: Eleven seconds. Two months of getting the paper flat enough to try.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (minimal, seed “standing-work”).
artworks.alt_text: Standing Work by Leo Zhang — Sumi ink on Xuan paper, minimalist and abstract
artworks.materials: Hand-ground sumi ink on Xuan paper

artworks.title: Hangzhou, Remembered
artworks.description: A soft indigo wash under two ink marks, the only work in his practice that references a place directly.
artworks.artist_note: The colour of the lake in the morning, as well as I can still recall it.
artworks.image_credit: Procedurally generated for this prototype (minimal, seed “hangzhou-remembered”).
artworks.alt_text: Hangzhou, Remembered by Leo Zhang — Sumi ink on Xuan paper, minimalist
